name: Mole
tagline: the burrower: the obstacle is the road
summary: The burrower. The whole game turned inside out: in open space it is slow (40 u/s) and turns badly; inside mass (within 16 u of any prism) it is fast (150 u/s), turns on a dime, and passes straight through. The course ribbon, the mass beside it, every rival's trail is a highway, and the more others lay, the faster you are. LT digs a tunnel of your own mass for the next lap; RT as you leave mass is a timed breach for a kick.

spec.v: fast inside mass, slow outside · LT dig · RT breach
momentum from terrain, inverted: wall-runs, grinds, 'the wall is the fast way'

fantasy: Everyone else dodges the prismscape; the Mole swims in it. A crowded cell is its ocean and an empty one its desert.
why: Titanfall taught that players use the wall when the wall is 2x faster; Mario Kart World's meta is grinding and wall-riding. The Mole makes mass the fast way on the game's own conserved prisms (a crowded cell is a valid state; this is the hull that wants one), and leaves tunnels others can follow: the Urchin rides ON prismscapes, the Mole goes THROUGH them.

charge.name: Breach
charge.tip: Charge is the kick of a timed breach.

mass.name: Wide Tunnel
mass.tip: Mass is the size of the tunnel prisms it digs.

space.name: Sense
space.tip: Space is how far from a prism still counts as inside mass.

time.name: Burrow Speed
time.tip: Time is its speed inside mass.

styles.name: Balanced
styles.info: Every element at 0: the recipe's numbers.

styles.name: Tunneller
styles.info: Wide tunnels, fast burrowing: builds the roads it then races on.

styles.name: Erupter
styles.info: Feels mass from far and breaches hard: the straight-line gambler.

styles.name: Maxed
styles.info: Every element at 10. A ceiling, not a match state.

notModelled: Passing through mass is a sphere test round the hull; the game's cradle (the Urchin's drape) is how mass would close over it visually.
A tunnel prism is ordinary conserved mass here: what it does to rivals' hulls (a reset) is the platform rule, not a Mole choice.
sources: Design: Docs/Studios/CONCEPT_FLEET.md (Mole). Nearest shipped relative: the Urchin's Trail Rider (URCHIN_TRAIL_RIDER.md), which rides the surface the Mole goes through.
